Rarity.rationale: Matches RippleBasin.cs:20. In the transcribed shared grab bag as Uncommon (relic_pools.py:128), executed by `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b13.py pool`.

CanonicalVars.rationale: RippleBasin.cs:22 is `new BlockVar(4m, ValueProp.Unpowered)` and BeforeSideTurnEnd passes the DynamicVar itself to CreatureCmd.GainBlock (line 32), so both the amount and the Unpowered prop travel together. The port passes 4 and ValueProp.UNPOWERED separately to BlockCmd.apply, which is the same pair. No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 4 is the non-ascension value.

BeforeSideTurnEnd.maps_to: on_player_turn_end (sts2_rl/relics/ripple_basin.py) -- the PLAIN phase of HookSystem's on_player_turn_end walk, run after the very_early and early passes (sts2_rl/hooks.py:153-180)
BeforeSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the phase passes are real. `HookSystem._each` walks the four phases very_early -> early -> plain -> late as COMPLETE separate listener passes whenever any current listener declares a phase variant of that hook (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36-38, 153-180), which is what Hook.cs's 24 multi-pass dispatchers do. The condition and the amount were already right; the SLOT is now a real plain pass that runs after every VeryEarly and Early listener.

AfterCardPlayed.maps_to: on_card_played (ripple_basin.py:32-34) -- which does real work the C# override does not
AfterCardPlayed.rationale: RippleBasin.cs:36-48's entire body, after the type and owner checks, is `base.Status = RelicStatus.Normal` -- presentation. C# needs no per-turn bookkeeping because BeforeSideTurnEnd queries the combat HISTORY instead: `History.CardPlaysFinished.Any(e => e.HappenedThisTurn(...) && e.CardPlay.Card.Type == Attack && e.CardPlay.Card.Owner == Owner)` (RippleBasin.cs:28). The sim substitutes a `_attack_this_turn` flag maintained from on_card_played (see guard N1 for why that substitution is equivalent today). Recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because the sim gives this hook behaviour the source does not have, so a future change to the sim's history or to on_card_played's firing rule would not be caught by looking at the C# override.

BeforeSideTurnStart.maps_to: on_player_turn_start (ripple_basin.py:29-30) -- again the flag reset, not C#'s presentation body
BeforeSideTurnStart.rationale: RippleBasin.cs:50-58's body after the participants check is `base.Status = RelicStatus.Active` -- presentation. The sim uses the slot to clear `_attack_this_turn`, which is the other half of the history substitution. The slot itself is turn_structure step 9 in C# and step 19 in the sim (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order`), but only a flag reset happens here and the first READER is on_player_turn_end, so the values agree at every observable point -- the same reasoning as relic/rainbow_ring's BeforeSideTurnStart in this batch and relic/brilliant_scarf's in batch 2.

AfterCombatEnd.maps_to: no counterpart; on_player_turn_start (ripple_basin.py:29-30) is the only reset
AfterCombatEnd.rationale: RippleBasin.cs:60-64 sets `base.Status = RelicStatus.Normal` and nothing else -- so, unlike relic/rainbow_ring, there is not even a counter for C# to zero here; the sim's dropped 'reset' is a dropped presentation update. `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` files ripple_basin in the 'RESET AT TURN START, BEFORE ANY READER (art_of_war shape -- genuinely safe)' bucket and prints `C# resets: ['AfterCombatEnd']`, which the corrected assignment column shows is `base.Status = RelicStatus.Normal`. TRACED TO THE FIRST READER as bug class 13 requires: `_attack_this_turn` can leave combat 1 True (a fight won on an attack skips the turn-end pass entirely -- combat.end_turn returns early once the phase is not PLAYER_TURN), and combat 2's own construction runs player.start_turn() -> on_player_turn_start, which clears it before any turn end can read it. Safe.

ExtraHoverTips.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / the N*Vfx nodes are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): C# runs BeforeTurnEnd as three complete ordered passes and the sim as one flat listener walk, so Orichalcum's deliberate two-phase snapshot loses to Ripple Basin's block on relic-pickup order
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the phase passes are real. `HookSystem._each` walks the four phases very_early -> early -> plain -> late as COMPLETE separate listener passes whenever any current listener declares a phase variant of that hook (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36-38, 153-180), which is what Hook.cs's 24 multi-pass dispatchers do. relic/orichalcum's snapshot now lives in `on_player_turn_end_very_early` (Orichalcum.cs:44-56) and Ripple Basin stays on the plain `on_player_turn_end` (RippleBasin.cs:26), so C#'s guarantee that the snapshot happens first holds whatever order the two were picked up in. WAS: one flat walk, so the answer was relic-pickup order -- 4 Block one way, 10 the other.

guards.what: N1: C# asks the combat HISTORY 'was an Attack finished this turn'; the sim keeps a boolean set from on_card_played
guards.rationale: Equivalent for every reachable case, checked clause by clause. (a) `HappenedThisTurn(Owner.Creature.CombatState)` is reproduced by the turn-start clear at ripple_basin.py:29-30, including on an extra turn (combat.end_turn increments `turn` and re-runs start_turn on the Pael's Eye path, so the flag clears there too). (b) `e.CardPlay.Card.Owner == base.Owner` is single-player-structural. (c) `e.CardPlay.Card.Type == CardType.Attack` matches ripple_basin.py:33. (d) The one real asymmetry is `CardPlaysFinished`: a play that STARTED but did not finish is absent from C#'s history, while the sim's on_card_played fires at the end of _resolve_card_play, so it too only records finished plays -- the same point, reached differently. (e) Auto-plays count on both sides: C# does not filter IsAutoPlay here (contrast PaelsEye.cs:155, which does, and BrilliantScarf.cs:84-87), and the sim's auto_play_card routes through the same card-play bracket. Recorded rather than skipped because a history-vs-flag substitution is exactly where PROMPT.md bug class 13 and the Pael's Eye G18 finding lived.

Both C# hooks fire for BOTH sides and the participants check narrows them to the player's own side turn; the sim's on_player_turn_end and on_player_turn_start are player-side-only dispatchers, so both are structurally satisfied. The enemy-side halves of those hooks are audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json guards G5/G11 and are not this record's to verdict.

guards.what: N3: `CreatureCmd.GainBlock(Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.Block, null)` (RippleBasin.cs:32) vs `BlockCmd.apply(hooks, player, 4, props=UNPOWERED)` (ripple_basin.py:39)
guards.rationale: Same target, same amount, same Unpowered prop -- so no Dexterity or block-multiplier scaling applies on either side, which is what Unpowered means and is why the relic gives exactly 4. The trailing null is the source card. Checked because a dropped UNPOWERED would make the relic scale with Dexterity and diverge silently on any turn the player holds some.
